overview.headline: How savings grow when interest earns interest

keyPoints.point: Students learn that compound interest means earning interest on saved money and on interest already earned.
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on the money you’ve saved and on the interest you earn along the way.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the Amount you start with of $1,000 is also called your principal.
keyPoints.quote: | Amount you start with | $1,000 | Also called your principal |

keyPoints.point: Students learn that 5 percent is the interest rate also called rate of return.
keyPoints.quote: | How much you earn | 5 percent | Also called your interest rate, or rate of return |

keyPoints.point: Students learn that adding to principal and increasing compounding frequency helps savings grow faster.
keyPoints.quote: Increasing the compounding frequency, finding a higher interest rate, and adding to your principal amount are ways to help your savings grow

keyTerms.gloss: Amount you start with that earns interest over time
keyTerms.quote: | Amount you start with | $1,000 | Also called your principal |

keyTerms.gloss: Percent you earn on principal each period as interest
keyTerms.quote: | How much you earn | 5 percent | Also called your interest rate, or rate of return |

keyTerms.gloss: How often compounding happens, such as once a year
keyTerms.quote: | How often you calculate interest | Once a year | Also called your compounding frequency |

keyTerms.gloss: Interest earned on savings and on previously earned interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on the money you’ve saved and on the interest you earn along the way.
